agent.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "I see a god coming up out of the earth.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

agent.problem: Stop 2, card 2 quotes "I am deeply distressed.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

agent.problem: Several non-opening story cards exceed two sentences: stop 1 cards 7 and 9 each have four, stop 1 card 11 has three when Saul's two quoted sentences are counted, and stop 2 card 19 has three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The question does not stand on its own once the preceding story card disappears. "This stranger" does not identify Saul, and "his request" does not say that he asked the medium to consult a spirit and bring someone up.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: seven of its ten choice cards are multiple choice, while the other three are true or false.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

agent.problem: Too many choices depend on discovery rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 5, 6 and 10 provide no basis for choosing David, Amalek or not eating; cards 13 and 18 likewise give no contextual basis for predicting Saul's immediate refusal or whether the group stays until morning. This is more than a few discovery questions and leaves only about half the stop's choices reasonably informed.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: "The elders of Endor" is an invented group, not a real detail from somewhere in the Bible, even though this is a who question.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

agent.problem: The walkthrough never clearly establishes that the woman served the food and that Saul and his servants ate. Card 18 places their eating inside a compound statement marked False, and this card clarifies only that they left. A baker could therefore miss, or even negate, the eating in verse 25.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
